text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Social Democrat party secretary general's proposal to loosen the ban on Sunday work has been met with widespread criticism. "That's completely out of the question," Fritz Verzetnitsch, head of Austria's trade union congress, said.
- Albania has rejected the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe's offer to send a fact-finding mission, headed by former chancellor Franz Vranitzky, to the troubled Balkan nation.
- Die Erste savings bank will take over AVZ's stake in GiroCredit for some 8.2 billion schillings.
- The EU Commission is expected to publish its decision on Bank Austria's takeover of rival Creditanstalt on Tuesday. Sources said the commission was likely to signal its approval.
- Following last year's boom in the insurance industry, insurers expect premium incomes to fall this year.
- Austrian Airlines reported record passenger figures for 1996. The company expects to report a profit for the year.
- State-owned tobacco monopoly Austria Tabak to be privatised via the stock exchange next year.
DIE PRESSE

- Takeover of GiroCredit makes Die Erste savings bank the country's second largest banking group after Bank Austria. Following the merger, the group will have total assets of about 601 billion schillings.
- The telecommunications industry rejects Transport Minister Caspar Einem's draft telecoms law, saying it does not provide the appropriate regulatory framework.
- Chancellor Viktor Klima says Austria will continue to implement tight border controls to fend off illegal immigrants.

- Klima, during an official visit to Germany, said Austria would not join NATO "in its current form." He was quoted as saying that "there is no reason to give up our neutrality and join NATO in its current form".
- Austria's tourism industry fails to decide on the introduction of a common reservation system.
- Bank Austria plans to merge its investment bank unit InvestmentBank Austria with that of Creditanstalt following the merger of the two banks.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank says Austria is not investing enough in Poland, says ongoing privatisation process in the country makes for good opportunities.
KURIER
- Car insurance premiums to fall as competition among insurers increases.
- Provincial energy provider Bewag plans to join a consortium with oil and chemicals group OMV and energy provider EVN in a bid to acquire gas provider Begas.
